meta.name: CodeAtlas Browser + Tool Verification Suite
meta.description: Comprehensive, layer-by-layer verification catalog for the CodeAtlas browser dashboard AND the MCP tool-call surface. Runs across EVERY repo in the catalog (43 framework repos + polar multi-repo + single-repo dogfood). Drives the live-verify protocol: drill-down correctness, adaptive labeling, diff/replay/tour, overlays, health, impact, multi-repo, re-init/resync stability, performance, MCP tool calls, and VSIX<->MCP parity. Each case is self-contained (route + steps + expected + how-to-verify) so it can be run by a human or an automated driver.
mandates: ALL REPOS: every applicable case runs against EVERY repo in `repoCatalog` (see `applicabilityRules` for how a case maps to repo categories/kinds). A case is not 'done' until it has evidence for each applicable repo.

SCREENSHOT EVERY TEST: every case MUST capture a screenshot and record an explicit ACTUAL-vs-EXPECTED visual observation — DOM/db/log/network checks are ADDITIONAL evidence, never a substitute for the screenshot. See `evidenceProtocol`.
TOOL CALLS INCLUDED: the MCP tool-call surface is a first-class dimension (suite `TOOLS`), exercised on the MCP build via JSON-RPC tools/call; each tool call also records expected-vs-actual output.

OUTPUT TO BUILD-NUMBERED tmp/: every test's evidence (screenshot, expected, actual, analysis, run-state) is written under `tmp/verification-runs/<build>/...` inside the repo. `tmp/` is already git-ignored (.gitignore), publish-ignored (.vscodeignore `tmp/**`), and VS Code-hidden (.vscode/settings.json).
notes: This is a verification CATALOG, distinct from the Playwright specs in e2e/tests/ (which run against mock handlers). These cases run against a REAL initialized workspace on the live browser dashboard.

Expected values marked with <observed> are workspace-specific snapshots captured on polar @ v9.0.30; treat the shape/relationship as the assertion, not the exact integer, unless the case says 'exact'.
Routes shown for specific repos (e.g. #/sequence/polar/...) are EXAMPLES. The runner substitutes per-repo entities discovered at run time — see `conventions.routeTemplates`.

'verify.method' lists the ADDITIONAL evidence beyond the mandatory screenshot: dom (query text/roles), db (sqlite3 on state.db/per-repo db), log (CodeAtlas output channel / daemon log), network (WS/CDP + JSON-RPC), perf (ext-host CPU/RSS + open latency).

vsix.label: VS Code extension (VSIX)
vsix.launch: code --install-extension <vsix> --force, then close+reopen VS Code on the workspace
vsix.notes: code --install-extension while VS Code is running does NOT reload; only close+install+reopen loads the new bundle.

mcp.label: MCP standalone daemon
mcp.launch: node dist/mcp-server.js <repo> (or claude mcp add); reset .codeatlas-sa/ to force fresh init
mcp.notes: Parity target: every VSIX case with builds including 'mcp' must behave identically. Prefer shared core/ modules over duplicated handler logic.

polar.purpose: Primary multi-repo dogfood: exercises distributed orchestrator, FE vs backend labeling, cross-repo edges, re-init/resync scale.

repoCatalog.description: Every repo the suite runs against. `npm run fetch:real-projects` clones the 43 framework repos into e2e/real-repos/ (gitignored). Detection baselines live in e2e/real-projects/expectations.json (refresh with npm run verify:real:update).

repos.note: 132 sub-repos — MCP-only; too heavy for the VS Code ext host.

baselineMetrics.description: Per-repo known-good detection thresholds live in e2e/real-projects/expectations.json and are INJECTED into each per-repo suite by the generator as `baseline`. DETECT cases assert the live browser/tool counts meet these. Refresh the baseline with `npm run verify:real:update` when detection intentionally changes.

fields.minApiCount: total entry points in apiIndex (HTTP + non-HTTP)
fields.minFlowGraphsWithDecision: L5 flows containing >=1 decision node (control-flow depth)
fields.minMobileItemCount: mobile screen/nav/network items (0 for backend repos)
fields.minAnonymousResolutionRate: fraction of anonymous route handlers resolved to a named symbol

capabilityMatrix.description: Per-repo DEFINING entry-point/feature capabilities (high-confidence from the repo's framework + CLAUDE.md detection table). The generator injects these as `capabilities` and includes a `capability`-tagged case ONLY when the repo has that capability — so each repo verifies its OWN entry-point kinds (no false failures for kinds a framework doesn't emit). Conservative by design: a listed capability MUST render; unlisted kinds are checked by the no-hallucination case.

outputLayout.description: Every test's evidence is written here. The folder is BUILD-NUMBERED and lives inside the repo under tmp/ (git-ignored, publish-ignored, VS Code-hidden).
outputLayout.buildNumber: the extension version under test + a run id, e.g. '9.0.30-run01' (or '9.0.30-<gitShortSha>'). One folder per run.

overall run: started/finished, both builds up?, repos covered, per-suite pass/fail/blocked tallies, skips (with reasons — no silent caps)
structure.tmp/verification-runs/<build>/summary.md: human-readable roll-up + cross-repo analysis + ticket list
structure.tmp/verification-runs/<build>/<repo>/<su: actual-vs-expected verdict + bug write-up on FAIL
additional artifacts: dom.txt, db.txt, log.txt, network.json, perf.json

ignored.vscode: .vscode/settings.json files.exclude + search.exclude hide tmp/ from the explorer + search

screenshot.appliesTo: EVERY case in EVERY suite (including TOOLS)
screenshot.rule: Capture at least one screenshot of the actual rendered state; multi-step cases capture before + after (NN-<label>.png). A case without a screenshot is INCOMPLETE regardless of other evidence.

actualVsExpected.rule: OBSERVE the screenshot, write actual.md, then analysis.md with an explicit PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict comparing actual to expected. DOM/db/log/network/perf checks are ADDITIONAL — they never replace the screenshot observation.

bothBuilds.rule: For cases with builds:['vsix','mcp'], capture a screenshot on EACH build (:7742 and :7842) and note parity in analysis.md.

toolCallEvidence.rule: TOOLS cases save the raw JSON-RPC request+response to evidence/network.json; when the tool drives a view (get_tour/get_impact_analysis/get_feature_pack/etc.), ALSO screenshot the rendered result.

onFailure.rule: On FAIL: keep the failing screenshot, capture the ext-host/daemon log tail, and write a ticket line (repro + finish-line + test scenario) into analysis.md AND the repo ISSUES.md.

applicabilityRules.description: Maps each case to the repos it must run against (from case.scope + case.tags), so we avoid a 45x70 hand-enumerated matrix. A case may carry an explicit `applicability` object to override.

byScope.per-service: all repos (compared within the repo's own category)

byTag.webhook: backend repos with a webhook provider (stripe/github/slack/twilio)

applicabilityRules.buildScope: builds:['vsix','mcp'] → run on BOTH; heavyReposMcpOnly run MCP-only (record the VSIX skip + reason in run-state.json — no silent caps).

toolCatalog.description: MCP tool-call surface exercised by suite TOOLS on the MCP build (JSON-RPC: initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call). Names extracted from src/mcp/mcp-tools.ts. Hidden tools (AGENT_HIDDEN_TOOLS) are exercised via tools/call directly even though they are not in the default agent-facing tools/list.
toolCatalog.howToCall: node dist/mcp-server.js <repo> over stdio; JSON-RPC: {method:'initialize'} -> {method:'tools/list'} -> {method:'tools/call', params:{name, arguments}}. Or via the connected client (claude mcp add <name> -- node dist/mcp-server.js <repo>).
toolCatalog.argValidation: callToolHandler validates required args (MCP-EVAL-3) — a missing required arg returns isError with 'missing required argument', not a crash.

runMatrix.description: Execution model: for each repo in repoCatalog, for each suite/case whose applicability includes that repo, run the case on the applicable build(s), capture the MANDATORY screenshot + actual-vs-expected, and write evidence under tmp/verification-runs/<build>/<repo>/<suiteId>/<caseId>/.

preRunReset.rule: BEFORE every repo run: `git -C <repoPath> checkout -- .` + `git -C <repoPath> clean -fd` to restore the repo to its ORIGINAL committed state (undo probe/feature files from prior runs). No run starts from a dirty tree. Then re-init + resync and capture the perf baseline (SETUP-04). After the run, reset again to drop probe files.
steps: re-init (time it, assert distributed for multi-repo, non-zero counts)
git checkout/clean again to clean up probe files

order: Bring up the build (VSIX close+install+reopen, or MCP daemon)
PRE-RUN RESET per repo: git checkout -- . + git clean -fd
Resync; TIME it + capture perf baseline
Walk browser suites L1..PARITY per repo (mandatory screenshot + actual-vs-expected each)
Run TOOLS suite on the MCP build
POST-RUN CLEANUP: git checkout/clean to drop probe files
runMatrix.coverageRule: A run is COMPLETE only when every applicable (repo x case) pair has a screenshot + verdict. Partial runs must list uncovered pairs in run-state.json.skips with reasons (no silent caps).

execution.description: TWO DECOUPLED PHASES so capture can run in PARALLEL (many browser sessions, one per repo) while a SEPARATE judge session evaluates the persisted artifacts and logs issues. This is the intended workflow: parallel capture in one or more sessions, judgment in a different session.

phase1_capture.role: Agent-TUNED capture (NOT fully mechanical). The Playwright runner (capture.mjs) provides deterministic primitives — navigate, click-by-text, screenshot, dump DOM/console, and a per-case ACTIONS DSL — but a TUNING AGENT supervises almost every run: it inspects the live DOM per repo/case, sets ACTIONS[caseId] with the right click targets (and file/git ops for modification cases), runs capture, reads capture.json.landed / _capture-manifest.json.needsTuning, and iterates until each interactive case lands on the correct layer. The agent does NOT evaluate correctness (that's the judge) and does NOT observe screenshots for pass/fail — it only makes the RUN accurate to the test.
phase1_capture.runner: SCOUT — e2e/browser-verification/scout.mjs (selection + roll-up; spawns the per-repo capture.mjs engine which carries the Playwright + ACTIONS DSL)

whoDoesWhat.deterministic (0 LLM): route navigation, screenshot, DOM/console dump, and any case whose ACTIONS already land (re-runs are free)
whoDoesWhat.tuning agent (LLM, NO vision): picks click targets/selectors per repo, authors ACTIONS for drills + modification cases (add-a-feature = fs.writeFile + git + click Sync), verifies landed==true, retries. This is why capture is NOT 0 tokens in practice.
whoDoesWhat.self-report signal: capture.json.landed (did a drill reach EXPECT_PREFIX, e.g. L5 -> #/flow/) + _capture-manifest.json.needsTuning tell the agent exactly what to fix.

phase1_capture.actionsDSL: ACTIONS[caseId] = [{goto}, {clickText, nth?}, {wait}, {shot}, {expectHashPrefix}] — the seam the tuning agent writes to. Modification cases add {writeFile}, {git}, {clickSync} (roadmap).
phase1_capture.parallelism: Launch N capture processes (one per repo) concurrently — each isolated by output dir. VSIX repos serialize on the single VS Code instance; MCP repos parallelize freely (one daemon per repo). Tuning can be one agent per repo.
writesPerRun: _capture-manifest.json — covered (with landed) | needsTuning (agent's worklist) | skipped(reason). No silent caps.
leavesForJudge: result.json (verdict) — filled by the judge, not capture

phase2_judge.role: Evaluative. A SEPARATE session/agent reads the captured artifacts, OBSERVES each screenshot (vision), compares to expected.md, writes actual.md + analysis.md (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED) + result.json, and logs every FAIL as an issue. Re-runnable without re-capturing; parallelizable (batch case folders across judges).
phase2_judge.runner: ARBITER — e2e/browser-verification/arbiter.mjs: `--plan` builds the judge worklist from captured artifacts, an agent judges (vision) following the rubric, then `--rollup` aggregates verdicts -> summary.md.
phase2_judge.screenshotVerification: MANDATORY — the judge bases actual.md on what it SEES in screenshot.png, not only dom.txt. A case with no screenshot is BLOCKED, never passed.
output: ISSUES.md line per FAIL (repro + finish-line + test scenario)

costModel.capture_deterministic: ~0 LLM for route-nav cases and any re-run whose ACTIONS already land (pure Playwright).
costModel.capture_tuning_agent: NOT 0. A tuning agent (browser-nav + DOM inspection, NO screenshot vision) authors/fixes ACTIONS for drills + modification cases until landed==true. Rough order: a few k tokens per interactive case the first time it's tuned, then ~0 on re-runs (ACTIONS are saved). Much cheaper than the inline run because there's no vision and no evaluation here.
costModel.judge: ~2-4k tokens per case (screenshot vision + expected + short verdict), batchable; a full-catalog judge pass ~= cases x ~3k ~= low tens of millions, and RE-RUNNABLE without the browser.
costModel.vs_inline: Still far cheaper than an inline agentic run (~80M): tuning has no vision, judging has no browser-turn context growth, and both phases are re-runnable — you pay tuning once per interactive case and judging is a compact {expected, screenshot, dom} triple.

routeTemplates.description: Repo-specific routes in cases are examples; substitute per-repo entities discovered at run time.

priority.P0: Core drill-down / stability / data-correctness — a failure blocks release.
priority.P1: Important feature correctness — a failure is a shipping bug.

diagramOpenMs.note: Render-only open of an already-built diagram (L1/L2b). 10-15s = a rebuild/grind bug.

reinitMultiRepoMs.note: Distributed re-init of polar (4 repos). Must NOT route to monolithic syncOrchestrator.

extHostIdleCpuPct.note: After init/resync settles; a pegged core + climbing RSS = synchronous O(n^2) / grind.
